title: Biological Compatibility Profile on Biomaterials for Bone Regeneration
protocol: Euthanize 1–2 day old neonatal pups by decapitation.
Place the heads in a Petri dish with sterile 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Hold the head by the nape of the neck, and cut the skin away using sterile scissors.

Incise the calvarium by piercing it (approximately 0.1–0.3 mm) with a pair of scissors that are then inserted underneath the calvarium in the back of the head at the base of the skull and cut along the calvarial edge laterally from back to front above the ears and then above the nasal bridge.

Incubate dissected calvaria with 8 mL of filter sterilized digestion solution (300 units/mL collagenase type IV and 2.14 units/mL dispase II dissolved in α-minimum essential medium (α-MEM)) in a 50 mL conical tube at 37 °C for 10 min in a shaking incubator at 200 shakes/min.
Discard the first supernatant.
Repeat the digestion procedure three times with 8 mL of digestion solution.
Collect the supernatant containing the cells after each digestion step.
Add collected supernatants to a 50 mL conical tube.
Store the 50 mL conical tube in an ice water bath until digestion completion (approximately 40 min).
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant using a Pasteur pipette attached to a vacuum pump.
Resuspend the cells in 40 mL of bone growth medium (BGM) containing α-MEM with 10% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum (FBS), and 1% penicillin-streptomycin solution.
Add 10 mL of cell suspension to each of four tissue culture plates (10 cm).
Culture the cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until confluence (2–3 days).
At confluence, aspirate the old medium from the tissue culture plates.
Wash the tissue culture plates once with 1x PBS (37 °C).
Aspirate the PBS from the tissue culture plates.
Add 2 mL of 1x trypsin solution containing 0.5% EDTA to each 10 cm tissue culture plate.
Incubate the tissue culture plates at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 5 min.
Check the plates with an inverted light microscope to ensure cells are detached from plastic.
Transfer all cell suspensions (total 8 mL) to a 50 mL conical tube containing 10 mL of fresh BGM.
Wash each plate with 5 mL of fresh BGM and transfer washings to the same 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 16 mL of fresh BGM.
Prepare 16 new 10 cm tissue culture plates, each containing 9 mL of BGM.
Add 1 mL of the cell suspension to each plate.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend in 10 mL of fresh BGM.
Count the cells and calculate the cell concentration.
Resuspend the cells in freezing medium containing 10% dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), 40% α-MEM, and 50% FBS.
Transfer 1.5 mL of the cell suspension to 2 mL cryovials for a total of 2 x 10^6 cells per vial.
Flash freeze the vials in liquid nitrogen for long-term storage in a liquid nitrogen tank.
Pre-incubate 14 mm diameter β-TCP disks in 1 mL of BGM in a 24-well suspension culture plate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Aspirate the pre-incubation medium from the plates.
Resuspend primary mouse OBs in BGM.
Add 4.4 x 10^4 OBs/cm^2 onto the pre-incubated β-TCP disks in a 24-well suspension culture plate and into a 24-well tissue culture plate for controls (1 mL/well).
Incubate the plates at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Change the medium every 2–3 days by aspirating old medium and adding 1 mL of fresh BGM to each well.
Transfer the β-TCP disks on days 7 and 14 to new wells to exclude signals from cells grown on suspension culture plates.
Aspirate the old medium from the wells on days 7 and 14.
Add 0.5 mL of BGM (37 °C) into each well.
Incubate the cultures for 30 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Add 55 µL of 10x cell proliferation reagent (1:10 dilution) directly into each culture well.
Prepare three wells containing 0.5 mL of BGM and 55 µL of the 10x cell proliferation reagent as blanks.
Incubate all plates for 30 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Withdraw 150 µL of supernatant from each well.
Transfer the withdrawn supernatant into a 96-well black plate.
Read fluorescence with excitation at 560 nm and emission at 590 nm.
Subtract blank readings from sample readings.
Pre-incubate 14 mm diameter β-TCP disks in 1 mL of BGM in a 24-well suspension culture plate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Aspirate the pre-incubation medium from the β-TCP disks.
Resuspend primary mouse OBs in BGM.
Add 8.8 x 10^4 OBs/cm² onto the pre-incubated β-TCP disks in a 24-well suspension culture plate and into a 24-well tissue culture plate for the control group (1 mL/well).
Replace the BGM with 1 mL of osteogenic mineralization medium (MM) containing BGM, 50 µg/mL ascorbic acid, and 5 mM β-glycerophosphate 24 h after adding OBs.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 14 days.
Change the medium every 2–3 days with 1 mL of freshly prepared MM to each well.
Aspirate the culture medium from the wells.
Wash the wells with 1 mL of sterile 1x PBS at 37 °C.
Carefully aspirate the PBS to retain attached cells on the tissue culture plastic or biomaterial.
Freeze the plates at -80 °C.
Thaw the control tissue culture plate and biomaterial suspension culture plate at room temperature (RT).
Transfer β-TCP disks into a new suspension culture plate for biomaterial samples.
Add 75 µL per well of the 1x cell lysis buffer to both plates.
Shake the plates for 5 min on a shaker at 400 shakes/min.
Transfer the cell lysate into a 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the samples at 300 x g for 6 min at RT.
Add 50 µL of the sample cell lysate supernatant to a 96-well black plate.
Add 50 µL of a solution consisting of 200 µM 6,8-difluoro-4-methylumbelliferyl phosphate (DiFMUP) fluorogenic substrate dissolved in 2x ALP buffer (pH 10) per well.
Set up two blank wells with 100 µL of a 1:1 solution containing 1x cell lysis buffer and 2x ALP buffer.
Prepare 8 reference standards with 100 μL/well using DiFMU ranging from 0.5 to 200 μM dissolved in a 1:1 solution of cell lysis buffer and ALP buffer.
Incubate the black plate at 37 °C for 15 min.
Read the fluorescence with excitation at 358 nm and emission at 455 nm.
Subtract the blank readings from the reference standards and sample readings.
Normalize ALP enzyme activity from cell lysates to total protein using a colorimetric assay for protein concentration.
Prepare BSA protein reference standards ranging from 0.05–2.5 µg/µL dissolved in 1x cell lysis buffer.
Add 5 μL of the sample cell lysate or 5 μL of BSA protein standard into a 96-well plate.
Add 25 μL of reagent A’ and 200 μL of reagent B to each well.
Set up two blank wells with 5 µL of 1x cell lysis buffer.
Incubate the plates at room temperature for 15 min.
Read the absorbance at 690 nm.
Subtract the blank readings from the reference standards and sample readings.
Stain ALP in cultured OBs on day 7 after adding MM to a control tissue culture plate and the biomaterial in a suspension culture plate.
Aspirate the culture medium from the wells.
Replace with 0.5 mL of 1x PBS (37 °C).
Aspirate the PBS.
Fix the cells by incubating in 0.5 mL of 10% buffered formalin at RT for 1 min.
Aspirate the 10% buffered formalin with a single-use pipet.
Add 0.5 mL of wash buffer (0.05% Tween20 in 1x PBS).
Dissolve one BCIP/NBT substrate tablet in 10 mL of ultrapure water and vortex until completely dissolved.
Aspirate the wash buffer.
Replace with 0.5 mL of BCIP/NBT substrate solution.
Incubate the plate at RT in the dark for 10 min.
Aspirate the staining solution.
Replace with 0.5 mL of wash buffer.
Transfer the stained β-TCP disks into a new well.
Scan the ALP-stained plates with a conventional flatbed scanner to record ALP staining.
Aspirate the culture medium from the wells containing primary OBs 14 days after the addition of MM.
Rinse twice with 0.5 mL of 1x PBS at RT.
Aspirate the PBS.
Fix the cells by adding 0.5 mL of the 10% buffered formalin solution at RT for 10 min.
Aspirate the 10% buffered formalin with a single-use pipet.
Wash twice with 0.5 mL of ultrapure water.
To the fixed OBs, add 0.25 mL of 40 mM ARS staining solution (pH 4.2) dissolved in ultrapure water.
Incubate the plate at RT for 10 min on a shaker at 100 shakes/min.
Aspirate the staining solution with a single-use pipet.
Rinse with 1 mL of ultrapure water.
Repeat rinsing step 5–10 times until colorless.
Aspirate the ultrapure water and add 1 mL of cold PBS.
Incubate the plate at RT for 10 min on a shaker at 100 shakes/min.
Aspirate the PBS, transfer the stained β-TCP disks to a new well.
Scan the plates with a flatbed scanner to record mineralization.
Add 0.25 mL of 10% cetylpyridinium chloride solution.
Incubate the plate at RT for 15 min on a shaker at 100 shakes/min.
Transfer the supernatants to a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 17,000 x g for 5 min at RT.
Add 10% cetylpyridinium chloride solution to the extracts with a dilution ratio of 1:10–1:20.
Add 300 µL samples into a 96-well plate including two blank wells containing only 10% cetylpyridinium chloride.
Prepare 7 ARS reference standards ranging from 4 to 400 µM by diluting the 40 mM ARS staining solution with 10% cetylpyridinium chloride solution.
Add 300 µL of the reference standard in duplicates to the 96-well plate.
Read the absorbance of the samples, blanks, and reference standards at 520 nm.
Subtract the blank readings from the reference standards and sample readings.
Clean segments of bone from the surrounding tissue.
Remove the trabecular bone and bone marrow.
Dry the bone at 50 °C for 24 hours.
Slice the bone into smaller chunks.
Cut the bone slices (approximately 300–350 µm thick) using a low-speed saw with a diamond blade.
Cut the 300–350 µm slices into quadratic disks (1 cm²).
Put the bone disks into a lockable glass vial and fill with distilled water.
Transfer the filled glass vial into an ultrasonic bath and sonicate for 5 minutes.
Repeat the sonication step three times using distilled water.
Pour off the distilled water, add 70% ethanol, and sonicate for 5 minutes.
Pour off the 70% ethanol and replace with 100% ethanol.
Store the bone slices in 100% ethanol at 4 °C for up to 4 weeks.
Irradiate the bone slices with UV light for 15 minutes on each side under sterile conditions.
Store the sterilized bone slices in a sterile culture plate at room temperature until further use.
Euthanize naïve 8–12 week old BALB/c mice using an intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of a solution containing 200 mg/kg ketamine and 24 mg/kg xylazine.
Remove the legs from mouse femurs and tibiae with sterile scissors at the hip joint.
Cut the limbs at the knee and ankle joints.
Remove soft tissue with sterile scalpel and forceps.
Cut off epiphyses.
Flush out and suspend the marrow with 1 mL BGM using a 27G needle attached to a 1 mL syringe in a 6 cm sterile Petri dish.
Add cell suspension to a 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the 6 cm Petri dish with 5 mL of BGM and transfer to the same 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 350 x g at 4 °C for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in OC differentiation medium (DM) containing BGM, 1 nM 1,25-(OH)2-vitamin D3, and 1 µM prostaglandin E2 (1 mL/well).
Pre-incubate 14 mm diameter β-TCP disks or bovine bone slices (1 cm²) in 1 mL of BGM in a 24-well suspension culture plate at 37 °C and 5% CO₂ for 24 h before adding cells.
Add 8.8 x 10⁴ cells/cm² of primary OBs suspended in BGM onto the biomaterials or control bone in a 24-well suspension culture plate or to a 24-well tissue culture plate.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO₂ for 24 h.
Add freshly isolated bone marrow OC precursors to the 24 h cultured primary OBs.
Culture the mixture at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 5 days.
Replace the medium with freshly prepared OC DM every other day.
Aspirate the culture medium from the control tissue culture plate and the biomaterial suspension culture plate.
Add 1 mL of 1x PBS (37 °C) to the plates.
Aspirate the PBS and fix the cells by incubating them in 1 mL of 10% buffered formalin solution at RT for 10 min.
Aspirate the 10% buffered formalin solution with a single-use pipet.
Add 1 mL of 1x PBS at RT to the plates.
Repeat this step three times.
Aspirate the PBS and replace with 1 mL of TRAP buffer (pH 5).
Incubate the plates at 37 °C for 30 min.
Aspirate the TRAP buffer and add 1 mL of 1:1 acetone and 100% ethanol to the plates.
Incubate the plate at RT for 30 s.
Quickly aspirate the acetone-ethanol solution with a single-use pipet.
Completely dry the plates at RT.
Prepare a 10 mg/mL naphthol-AS-MX phosphate stock solution in N,N-dimethylformamide.
Dissolve 0.6 mg/mL of fast red violet salt in TRAP buffer.
Add 0.1 mL of naphthol-AS-MX phosphate stock solution to 10 mL of fast red violet salt in TRAP buffer.
Add 1 mL of TRAP staining solution and incubate the plate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Aspirate the TRAP staining solution.
Add 1 mL of ultrapure water to stop the reaction.
Transfer the β-TCP disks and bovine bone slices after staining into a new well.
Observe red stained OCs using a light microscope (magnification: 10X).
Enumerate TRAP+ mature OCs with three or more nuclei.
Inject 0.1 mg/kg buprenorphine subcutaneously (s.c.) into 8-week old BALB/c mice for analgesia.
Anesthetize the mice with a mixture of 100 mg/kg ketamine and 5 mg/kg xylazine i.p.
Add a gel or ointment to the eyes to keep them moist.
Place the mouse on a heating plate at 37 °C during the entire procedure to prevent hypothermia.
Assess the anesthesia depth by toe and tail pinch.
Shave the fur on the top of the head between the ears and clean the surface with 7.5% povidone iodine solution and 70% ethanol.
Make a midline sagittal incision on the top of the skull between the ears with a sterile scalpel to expose the calvarium.
Remove the pericranium connective tissues above the right parietal bone by scraping it with a scalpel.

Create a critical-sized defect in the right parietal bone using a sterile dental trephine with a diameter of 4 mm (2000 rpm) under constant irrigation with normal saline solution to notch the right parietal bone and cut through the ectocortex and some endocortex.
Use a small periosteal elevator to break through the remaining endocortex.
Carefully lift the calvarial bone up and remove it with forceps.
Fill the resulting defect with pre-soaked β-TCP/C foam using forceps.
Put 0.5 µL of tissue adhesive at the edge of the defect at two opposite points.
Close the skin with a non-absorbable suture.
Clean all surgical instruments with cold sterilant to maintain sterile conditions before performing the next surgery on an anesthetized mouse.
Place the animals on a dry and clean heating plate at 37 °C in the surgery area for appropriate monitoring during the recovery period.
Monitor the respiratory rate, body temperature and color of mucous membranes and eyes every 10 min until they wake.
Transfer the operated conscious mice into a cage with food and water separated from the other animals until full recovery.
Inject 0.1 mg/kg buprenorphine s.c. for post-surgical analgesic therapy twice per day for 72 h.
Return fully recovered mice to their cages.
Euthanize the mice i.p. with a solution of 200 mg/kg ketamine and 24 mg/kg xylazine to determine the effectiveness of the biomaterial.
Decapitate the euthanized mouse with sharp scissors at 8–12 weeks post-implantation.
Fix the decapitated mouse head in 30 mL of 4.5% buffered formalin for 1-2 weeks.
Transfer fixed heads into 70% ethanol for long-term storage at 4 °C.
Use micro computed tomography (microCT) or standardized undecalcified histological techniques to evaluate bone regeneration.
Dehydrate the heads in ascending grades of ethanol and embed in glycol methyl methacrylate.
Cut glycol methyl methacrylate-embedded blocks with a diamond saw.
Grind sections to a thickness of approximately 80–100 µm for undecalcified histology.
Evaluate Levai Laczko stained bone sections to identify new bone formation.
Euthanize naïve 8-week old BALB/c mice i.p. with a solution of 200 mg/kg ketamine and 24 mg/kg xylazine.
Place the mouse on its right side, shave the fur on the left side, and clean the skin over the left side of the abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Make a 10 mm long and 1 mm deep incision in the skin of the mouse on the left side posteriorly following the ribs over the stomach using sterile scissors.
Open the skin and expose the peritoneum under sterile conditions.
Make a 10 mm long incision into the peritoneum using scissors, less than 1 mm deep.
Push the stomach proximally to expose the spleen.
Hold the spleen gently with sterile forceps.
Remove the spleen by cutting the tissue and vessels attached below it.
Place the intact spleen into a 50 mL tube containing 10 mL of cold 1x sterile PBS.
Prepare a single cell suspension by mincing the spleen using 2 sterile forceps or 2 sterile glass slides.
Pass the minced material through a sterile 40 μm cell strainer with cold 1x PBS using the plunger of a 1 mL syringe to remove debris.
Centrifuge the single cell suspension at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C in a 50 mL conical tube, aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of red blood cell (RBC) lysis buffer.
Incubate the cell suspension for 14 min at room temperature (RT).
Stop the reaction by adding 45 mL of Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RPMI) medium.
Centrifuge the cells after the cell lysis at 300 x g for 10 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend splenocytes in RPMI medium containing 10% heat-inactivated FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin solution, 0.1% gentamicin, 0.2% ß-mercaptoethanol, and 1% non-essential amino acids.
Pre-incubate β-TCP/C foam in a 96-well sterile culture plate containing RPMI medium for 24 h at 37 °C and 5% CO2 before cell seeding.

Add splenocytes at titrated numbers, e.g., 1.25 x 10^5, 2.5 x 10^5 and 5 x 10^5/well to wells in a 96-well tissue culture plate containing RPMI medium and additives, with or without the pre-incubated β-TCP/C foam.
Add 10 µg/mL concanavalin A (Con A) dissolved in medium for a total of 100 µL/well to the appropriate wells.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 72 h.
Measure cell proliferation with a bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU) assay.
Add 10 µL/well of BrdU labeling solution at 48 h of cell culture.
Incubate the plate for an additional 24 h.
At 72 h, collect the supernatant and store at -20 °C until further use.
Add 200 µL/well of the fixation solution to each well.
Incubate for 30 min at RT.
Aspirate the fixation solution.
Add 100 µL/well of the anti-BrdU antibody working solution and incubate for 90 min.
Aspirate the antibody solution, rinse the wells three times with 200–300 µL/well of washing solution and remove the washing solution.
Add 100 µL of substrate solution and incubate for 3–10 min at RT.
Measure the absorbance at 450 nm.
Measure interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-2 (IL-2), interleukin-4 (IL-4) and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) in the collected supernatants using a standard ELISA.
Anesthetize female 6-8-week old BALB/c mice with a mixture of 100 mg/kg ketamine and 5 mg/kg xylazine i.p.
Add gel or ointment to the eyes to keep them moist.
Place the mouse on a heating plate at 37 °C during the entire procedure.
Assess the anesthesia depth by toe and tail pinch.
Shave the abdominal fur.
Clean with 7.5% povidone iodine solution and 70% ethanol.
Make an 8 mm long midline incision through the skin along the linea alba.
Make a small incision into the peritoneum using a scalpel.
Place sterile PBS soaked β-TCP/C foam grafts (2x2x2 mm3) into the peritoneal cavity or without added materials for the age-matched sham control mice.
Suture the peritoneum and skin with absorbable and non-absorbable suture, respectively.
Clean all surgical instruments with cold sterilant to maintain sterile conditions before performing the next surgery on an anesthetized mouse.
Place the animals on a dry and clean heating plate at 37 °C in the surgery area for appropriate monitoring during the recovery period.
Monitor the respiratory rate every 10 min until they wake.
Monitor body temperature every 10 min until they wake.
Monitor color of mucous membranes every 10 min until they wake.
Monitor eyes every 10 min until they wake.
Transfer the operated conscious mice into a cage with food and water separated from the other animals until full recovery.
Return fully recovered mice to their cages.
Inject 0.1 mg/kg buprenorphine s.c. if the operated animals show signs of pain.
Euthanize mice 7 days post-implantation with a solution of 200 mg/kg ketamine and 24 mg/kg xylazine i.p.

Lavage peritoneal cavity using a 1 mL syringe with a 25G needle for a total of 3 mL of cold PBS by holding the mouse head down and inserting the needle in the left lower abdominal quadrant aiming proximally.
Centrifuge the peritoneal lavage fluid at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant to store at -20°C for ELISA measurements of IL-1β, IL-2, and IL-4 cytokines.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of PBS.
Count the peritoneal cells using trypan blue on a hemocytometer.
Cytocentrifuge the cell suspension at 5 x 10^5 cells onto glass slides, allow the slides to dry and stain for differential cell count.
Using a light microscope, count a minimum of 300 cells in total and differentiate between macrophages, eosinophils, neutrophils, and lymphocytes.
Anesthetize female 6–8 week old BALB/c mice with a mixture of 100 mg/kg ketamine and 5 mg/kg xylazine i.p.
Add gel or ointment to the eyes to keep them moist.
Place the mouse on a heating plate at 37 °C during the entire procedure to prevent hypothermia.
Assess the anesthesia depth by toe and tail pinch.
Place the mouse on its back.
Shave the abdominal fur.
Clean the shaved surface with 7.5% povidone iodine solution.
Clean the shaved surface with 70% ethanol.
Make an 8 mm long midline incision through the skin along the linea alba of the abdomen using a scalpel.
Implant PBS soaked biomaterial (2x2x2 mm3) under the skin or add no materials for the age-matched sham control mice.
Suture the skin with a non-absorbable suture.
Clean all surgical instruments with cold sterilant to maintain sterile conditions before performing the next surgery on an anesthetized mouse.
Place the animals on a dry and clean heating plate at 37 °C in the surgery area for appropriate monitoring during the recovery period.
Monitor the respiratory rate, body temperature and color of mucous membranes and eyes every 10 min until they wake.
Transfer the operated conscious mice into a cage with food and water separated from the other animals until full recovery.
Return fully recovered mice to their cages.
Inject 0.1 mg/kg buprenorphine s.c. if the operated animals show signs of pain.
Euthanize mice i.p. with a solution of 200 mg/kg ketamine and 24 mg/kg xylazine when ready to examine the implantation site.
Excise the implantation site with surrounding tissue (1 cm²) eight weeks post-implantation.
Fix the excised tissue in 4.5% buffered formalin overnight.
Embed fixed tissue in paraffin.
Cut paraffin-embedded tissue into 4 μm sections.
Stain 4 μm paraffin-embedded tissue sections with Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) for inflammation or Masson’s trichrome for collagen deposition and fibrosis.
